title: Flying Demon (R1/P1) proven capture — original-arcade user-play trace analysis
analysis_scope: trace analysis only; NO palette 16-color decode, NO Round-2 boss work, NO production/ROM change, Build counter unchanged
method: 34485-row dedup actor-state trace; per-block/base/+0x3E presence profiling; encounter windows record==8 (frames 6318-11120) and record==13 (frames 14262-16726); actor_508 slot/piece/state correlation

identity.conclusion: PROVEN-BY-STRUCTURE: the Flying Demon is the SPECIAL two-slot actor_508 composite (base 0x0129), NOT a +0x3E family-table enemy.
identity.base_code: 0x0129 (direct sprite base; NOT an entry in the +0x3E family table 0x45502)
identity.why_not_plus3e_family: actor_508 fields are +0x3E=0x00, +0x38=0x00, +0x752=0x00, +0x27(attr)=0x80 for ALL 1876 rows. It carries none of the FUN_0004544e 12-row family-table selection (base 0x0129 is not a table base; attr lacks the 0x40 family-palette flag, uses 0x80). The Flying Demon is handled by the dedicated actor_508 special path, outside the ordinary enemy +0x3E family system.
identity.prior_guess_withdrawn: sprites.json actor_3e 'one of {4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11}' is WITHDRAWN — the demon does not use the +0x3E family selector at all.

task_answers.1_actor_plus3e_family: NONE — +0x3E=0x00 (special actor_508 path, not a family-table enemy). Identity = actor_508 block + base 0x0129.
task_answers.2_plus38_plus752_state: +0x38=0x00, +0x752=0x00 (both zero for all rows; the demon does not use the +0x38/+0x752 sub-form selection).
task_answers.3_component_A_ownership: component_A @0x0010C508 (actor_508 idx0), PC090OJ/OBJ SAT records 57-69, codes 0x0129-0x0155.
task_answers.4_component_B_ownership: component_B @0x0010C548 (actor_508 idx1), PC090OJ/OBJ SAT records 70-82, codes 0x014A-0x0177. BODY-vs-WINGS now PROVEN BY RENDER (enemy contact-sheet task): component_A draws the BODY (torso/legs/sword), component_B draws the two WINGS. Neutral component_A/B identifiers retained. Evidence: contact_sheets/r1p1_enemies_diagnostic.png.
task_answers.5_component_relationship: TWO separate actor structures (two distinct addresses, two disjoint SAT owned ranges), co-located and state-locked, forming ONE Flying Demon enemy. Not a single actor with a piece sub-group. NOT the previously-hypothesized a5+0x748/a5+0x8c8 aux blocks (those carry small unrelated effects here).
task_answers.6_pc090oj_record_ownership: component_A = OBJ records 57-69 (0x39-0x45). component_B = OBJ records 70-82 (0x46-0x52). Death animation (codes 0x0288-0x02A8) is written into these same records by both components together.
task_answers.7_damage_lifecycle: STRONGLY COUPLED / STATE-LOCKED across the captured lifecycle. The two components share the IDENTICAL observed state every frame (states 0x03 spawn -> 0x04,0x05,0x06,0x07,0x08,0x09 living -> 0x0F death) and despawn on the SAME frame (16784). Co-occurrence: (09,09)x241 (05,05)x199 (06,06)x145 (08,08)x113 (04,04)x87 (07,07)x75 (0F,0F)x23 (03,03)x2.
task_answers.8_wing_only_death_arcade: NOT OBSERVED. In 885 shared frames there are ZERO frames where one component is in death-state 0x0F while the other is in a living state; the trace shows a state-locked lifecycle throughout. This is strong evidence but NOT a universal-impossibility proof: the saved trace contains no positively-identified attack against a single component, and no static arcade damage-ownership code was analyzed. Exact damage/death ownership remains DEFERRED.
